criteria.notes: Operations pulse: three headline metrics with deltas, an hourly throughput series, and a daily-target gauge with unit context.
Operations-centre concept retained: metric tiles above a dominant time series, live indicator in the header.

A conventional operations layout, which is what this example teaches: metric tiles, one time series and a target gauge. It is deliberately the plainest example in the portfolio rather than a styled one.
Metric values dominate their tiles and clear the room-distance floor; axis labels sit at the metadata role by intent.
Light-theme scenario preserves chart line, fill and gauge contrast against the pale field.
Long-label scenario keeps metric captions complete by wrapping within the tile rather than ellipsizing the value.
Tiles and chart divide the surface at every aspect; portrait and square restack rather than compress, and the empty state substitutes a centred no-signal message.
Chart renders crisply at every surface with no raster media; the gauge track and fill stay aligned.
Shares the dark panel language with other operational examples, which is appropriate to its brief, but its metric-plus-series structure is not duplicated elsewhere.
